title: Periodic Quarter-Wave UV Bragg Reflector
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack centered at 300 nm will produce a photonic bandgap with high reflectance in 200-400 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 800-1500 nm due to the wavelength scaling of Bragg resonance.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high-reflectance bands centered at the design wavelength λ0 where each layer has optical thickness λ0/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than λ0 (here 800-1500 nm vs 300 nm), the stack becomes increasingly transparent as the optical thicknesses become sub-quarter-wave.
soft_objectives: Minimize layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: Quarter-wave thicknesses at 300 nm are manufacturable with standard deposition
HfO2/SiO2 pair has established deposition processes per L05
theory_basis: Bragg reflection condition for periodic multilayers
Photonic bandgap formation in quarter-wave stacks
expected_advantages: Simple periodic structure reduces optimization complexity
28 layers provides strong UV reflection with margin under 30-layer limit
known_risks: Periodic structure may create secondary reflection bands in SWIR
Quarter-wave at 300 nm may not optimally balance both bands
Fixed periodicity limits ability to fine-tune spectral edges
execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer stack on fused_silica substrate with air incidence. Stack topology: 14 repeated pairs of hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) (28 layers total), starting with hfo2 adjacent to air. Initial layer thicknesses: hfo2 at 75 nm, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) at 125 nm (quarter-wave optical thickness at 300 nm center wavelength). Optimization variables: scale factor applied uniformly to all layer thicknesses (range 0.8-1.2), and individual thickness adjustments per layer type within ±20% of scaled baseline. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Wavelength bands: 200-400 nm (maximize reflectance), 800-1500 nm (maximize transmittance). Material refractive indices from measured datasets for hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos). Total layer count fixed at 28.
